text.p: Trading in Sweden's state-controlled bank Nordbanken was suspended on Wednesday morning at the bank's request with more information to be released later today, the Stockholm bourse said.
The Swedish government currently holds 65.5 percent of the bank and has previously indicated it is planning to sell its stake.
A Finance Ministry spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday that no decision had yet been made on the date of the sale.
Nordbanken said it would hold a press conference at 1130 GMT.
Nordbanken posted an 18 percent hike in profit after credit losses in the first half of 1996 of 3.80 billion crowns.
A sharp 61 percent drop in credit losses to 260 million crowns against 661 million crowns in the first half of 1995 was the main reason for the improved profits.
Financial markets have speculated that mortgage institute Stadshypotek would be a ripe target for banks looking to expand, tipping Nordbanken as the bank most likely to succeed.
The state had said it hoped to dispose of its 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek by the end of December.
Stadshypotek's home loan business would help Nordbanken compete with arch-rival Swedbank in this lucrative area.
